Selection Structures
A selection structure allows a program to choose
between different paths of code.
Instead of always running every line in order, the
program checks a condition and decides what
should happen next.
In Python, selection structures are commonly
created using if, elif, and else.

Ordering Conditions
When several conditions overlap, their order matters
because Python stops at the first condition that is True.
For conditions such as score >= 80, score >= 65, and
score >= 50, the most restrictive condition should
come first and the broadest condition should come last.
A score of 95 satisfies all three conditions, so if
score >= 50 appears first, Python will stop there and
never reach the more specific checks.

Conditions and Statements Wrap Up
Selection structures allow programs to make decisions by
evaluating conditions as True or False.
if checks the first condition, elif allows additional conditions
to be checked, and else handles any remaining case.
Comparison operators create many common conditions,
while not can reverse a condition.
Because Python checks an if / elif structure from top to
bottom, overlapping conditions must be ordered carefully.
